description: GRAPH-NATIVE SURPRISE GATE (block 284000). A decision fires on SURPRISE -- observation != held social prediction -- as RULES, not a Python dict. A resident holds a SocialPrediction as predicts_near edges; the adapter mints observation as sees edges (proximity). sg_surprise: a sees with no matching predicts_near sets m.surprised=1 (the prediction residual, computed by a rule) -- a PREDICTED co-presence fires nothing. sg_absorb: the same unpredicted sees adds predicts_near, so the prediction absorbs the surprise (held-prediction update). m.surprised gates the conduct collapse (282000): only a surprised resident decides; between surprises it continues its durative action. Edge-absence uses the standard Not(Exists(Neighbours...==o)) form. This is the graph-native realization of block 283000's Python time-model demonstrator, composing with the supergraph town. ZERO new Rust; self_load_only.

rules.name: sg_provide_directed
rules.comment: DIRECTED affordance provision: a directed option is afforded (impulse := base_weight) iff ITS OWN target is co-present (matches d aims_at o AND m sees o). Unlike the target-agnostic 280000 aff_provide rules, harm@B is offered only when B is seen, not when anyone is -- required once options are pre-minted toward every resident.

rules.name: sg_surprise
rules.comment: SURPRISE = observation != held prediction, as a rule. A `sees` edge to an other NOT in predicts_near sets m.surprised=1 -- the prediction residual. A PREDICTED co-presence (predicts_near present) does not match, so it fires no surprise. m.surprised is the gate the conduct collapse (282000) reads: only a surprised resident decides.

rules.name: sg_absorb
rules.comment: The prediction ABSORBS the surprise: the unpredicted other is added to predicts_near, so re-seeing it next tick is no longer surprising (held-prediction update -- the perception held-surface analog). Same match as sg_surprise, so both fire on the residual in one fixpoint; next tick the residual is gone.
